anomalies.observed: Both VSS pins of the NAVC MCU (pins 18 and 63) sit on an auto-named net, 'Net-(NAVC1-VSS-Pad18)', that contains no GND connection. VSSA (pin 12) is a single-pin unconnected net. The FCC1 MCU, by contrast, has all its VSS pins (10, 26, 49, 74, 99) and VSSA (pin 19) on GND.
anomalies.expected: All VSS and VSSA pins of the STM32F405 should return to the common GND net, as they do on the FCC1 MCU. The NAVC MCU's ground is otherwise unconnected, so the chip has no reference.
anomalies.impact: With its ground pins floating, the NAVC MCU cannot be referenced to the board ground. It would fail to run or behave erratically, and the NAVC-side sensors and GPS would lose their reference.

anomalies.observed: The LDO output (REG2 pin 1) and the sensor supplies sit on net '+3.3V', while the MCU supply pins, the FCC decoupling, the I2C pull-ups and the NAVC decoupling sit on a separate net named '+3V3'. Nothing in the netlist joins the two nets.
anomalies.expected: A single 3V3 rail fed from the LDO should supply the MCUs, the I2C pull-ups and the sensors. The specification states that 3V3 feeds both MCUs and all I2C sensors.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: If the two nets are truly separate, the MCUs and pull-ups would have no regulated 3.3 V supply. This may be a labelling artefact of the export, so confidence is low.

parsed.summary: The NAVC1 MCU's VSS and VSSA pins are not tied to GND, unlike the FCC1 MCU, which leaves that processor without a ground reference. A lower-confidence concern is that the 3.3 V supply is split across two unconnected net names.
